# Qwen Model Family: Architecture Evolution

## Overview

Qwen model family evolves from dense to MoE + hybrid attention. This skill focuses on architectural differences relevant to the ANDL distributed inference engine.

| Model | Type | Attention | MoE | llama.cpp class |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen2 | Dense | Full attention only | No | `llm_build_qwen2` |
| Qwen2-MoE | MoE | Full attention only | Yes (60 experts) | `llm_build_qwen2moe` |
| Qwen3 | Dense | Full attention only | No | `llm_build_qwen3` |
| Qwen3-MoE | MoE | Full attention only | Yes (128 experts) | `llm_build_qwen3moe` |
| Qwen3.5 | Hybrid | Full + Linear (SSM/GDN) | No | `llm_build_qwen35` |
| Qwen3.5-MoE | Hybrid | Full + Linear (SSM/GDN) | Yes (128 experts) | `llm_build_qwen35moe` |
| Qwen3.5-MoE-122B | Hybrid | Full + Linear (SSM/GDN) | Yes (256 experts, 48L) | `llm_build_qwen35moe` |
| **Qwen3.6-MoE** | **Hybrid** | **Full + Linear (SSM/GDN)** | **Yes (256 experts)** | **`llm_build_qwen36moe`** |

## Qwen3.6-35B-A3B — Target Model for ANDL

### Architecture Highlights

```
Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (Activated 3 Billion)
├── 40 layers total
│   ├── 10 Full Attention layers (layer % 4 == 3: 3,7,11,15,19,23,27,31,35,39)
│   └── 30 Linear Attention layers (SSM/GDN: conv + QKV + delta net)
├── Each layer: Post-attention norm + MoE FFN + Shared Expert
├── GQA (Grouped Query Attention): 16 Q heads, 2 KV heads
├── 256 experts, top-8 + shared expert
├── Q/K per-head normalization (attn_q_norm, attn_k_norm) on full-attention layers
├── IMRoPE (Interleaved Multi-section Rotary Position Embedding)
└── Derived from: llm_build_delta_net_base
```

### Key Parameters (from GGUF metadata — NOT hypothetical)

```
hidden_dim (n_embd):          2048
intermediate_dim:             512    (expert_feed_forward_length, NOT ~1536!)
shared_intermediate_dim:      512    (expert_shared_feed_forward_length)
head_dim (rope):              128    (hidden_dim / n_head = 2048 / 16 = 128)
n_head (Q):                   16
n_head_kv (K,V):              2      → GQA ratio 8:1
head_dim_norm:                256    (Q/K norm weight size — per Q+gate block)
n_layer:                      40
n_expert:                     256
n_expert_used (top_k):        8
full_attention_interval:      4     (every 4th layer is Full Attention)
rope_type:                    IMRoPE (GGML_ROPE_TYPE_IMROPE = 40)
rope_dimension_count:         64
rope_sections:                [11, 11, 10, 0]  // 4-section IMRoPE, sum=32 < rope_dimension_count=64
norm_type:                    RMSNorm
ffn_type:                     SiLU-gated (SwiGLU)
context_length:               262144
vocab_size:                   ~248320
```

### SSM Parameters (from GGUF metadata)

ssm.group_count (n_k_heads):  16
ssm.time_step_rank (dt_rank): 32
ssm.conv_kernel (d_conv):     4
```

### Expert Sharding Strategy (ANDL)

256 experts ÷ 8 shards = 32 experts per shard.
Per-layer per-shard expert data: ~154+154+177 = ~485 MB (quantized).
All 40 layers per shard: ~19.4 GB total → **~2.4 GB per expert shard**.
All 8 shards: ~19.1 GB total expert weights.

Global Node total (embed + output + all attention + SSM + norms + routers + shared experts): **~2.5 GB**.

## Hybrid Attention System

### Layer Type Determination

```cpp
if (hparams.is_recurrent(il)) {
    // LINEAR ATTENTION LAYER: SSM/DeltaNet
    cur = build_layer_attn_linear(inp->get_recr(), cur, il);
} else {
    // FULL ATTENTION LAYER: Q/K/V + IMRoPE + sigmoid gate
    cur = build_layer_attn(inp->get_attn(), cur, inp_pos, sections, il);
}
```

The `is_recurrent(il)` check is determined by model hyperparameters loaded from GGUF metadata.

### Full Attention Layer (`build_layer_attn`)

```
Input → Q projection (wq) → Q/K Norm (attn_q_norm, attn_k_norm)
      → K projection (wk)  → IMRoPE on Q, K
      → V projection (wv)  → Attention compute
                           → Sigmoid gate (from Q projection's gate channel)
                           → Output projection (wo)
```

Key details:
- **Q projection outputs Q + gate**: `wq` shape is `[n_head * head_dim * 2, hidden_dim]` — the extra `head_dim` per head is the gate channel
- **Q/K normalization**: Q and K are individually RMS-normalized after projection (unique to Qwen3.5/3.6)
- **Sigmoid gating**: The gate channel is sigmoid-activated and multiplied element-wise with attention output

### Linear Attention Layer (`build_layer_attn_linear`)

```
Input → Merged QKV projection (wqkv) + Gate (wqkv_gate)
      → Beta projection (ssm_beta) → Sigmoid
      → Alpha projection (ssm_alpha) → Softplus → × ssm_a = gate
      → Conv1D (ssm_conv1d) on QKV
      → Q/K/L2-normed, split from conv output
      → DeltaNet attention (build_delta_net)
      → Gated normalization: norm(output, z) where z = silu(wqkv_gate)
      → Output projection (ssm_out)
```

This is a **gated delta net** (GDN) — a type of linear attention / state space model. It's computed on the Global Node, not distributed to experts.

### Convolution State Cache

Linear attention layers maintain a persistent conv state between tokens:
```cpp
conv_states_all  // shape: [(conv_kernel_size-1)*conv_channels, n_seqs]
ssm_states_all   // shape: [head_v_dim*head_v_dim*num_v_heads, n_seqs]
```

These are stored in `llm_build_delta_net_base`'s memory system and updated per-token via `ggml_cpy`.

## MoE Routing: Load-Balanced (Near-Uniform)

**Qwen3.6's routing is load-balanced by design.** Profiling on 468K tokens (626+ requests) from the iic/ms_agent dataset confirms near-perfect uniformity:

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Per-layer entropy | 7.68 bits (96% of theoretical max 8.0) |
| Experts used per layer | 256/256 — ALL used |
| Max expert hits | 23-24 (per request window) |
| Min expert hits | 12 |
| **Cold/hot ratio** | **Only 2:1** |
| 80% coverage needs | **~195/256 experts** (76%) |
| 95% coverage needs | **~239/256 experts** (93%) |
| 99.9% coverage needs | ~255/256 experts |
| Top-1 expert traffic share | ~0.5% |

**Layer 39 is special:** only 28/256 experts used, with just 96 total hits — this is the final layer and receives far fewer tokens due to early termination in the profiling corpus.

This means **hot/warm/cold expert tiering is ineffective for Qwen3.6** — ~76% of experts must be "hot" to cover even 80% of traffic. Compare to DeepSeek-V3 where ~15% of experts cover 80% of traffic with entropy ~5.5 bits. The model was trained with strong load-balancing loss to prevent router collapse.

For tiered deployment, consider models with more skewed routing (DeepSeek V3, Mixtral) or accept that Qwen3.6 needs all experts readily accessible. The practical approach for 16GB GPUs is **streaming per-layer** — keep all 256 experts in CPU RAM (192GB is plenty), load one layer's experts to GPU per inference step.

## MoE FFN Layer (`build_layer_ffn`)

```cpp
// 1. MoE expert routing (on Global Node)
moe_out = build_moe_ffn(cur,
    ffn_gate_inp,          // Router weight [256, 2048]
    ffn_up_exps,           // Expert up projections
    ffn_gate_exps,         // Expert gate projections
    ffn_down_exps,         // Expert down projections
    n_expert=256, n_expert_used=8,
    LLM_FFN_SILU,          // SiLU activation
    true,                  // use shared expert
    expert_weights_scale,  // from hparams
    LLAMA_EXPERT_GATING_FUNC_TYPE_SOFTMAX  // routing uses softmax
);

// 2. Shared expert (on Global Node)
if (ffn_up_shexp != nullptr) {
    ffn_shexp = build_ffn(cur, ffn_up/gate/down_shexp, LLM_FFN_SILU, LLM_FFN_PAR);
    shared_gate = sigmoid(ffn_gate_inp_shexp @ cur);  // token-level gate
    ffn_shexp = ffn_shexp * shared_gate;
    cur = moe_out + ffn_shexp;  // ADDITIVE merge!
}

// Note: In ANDL distributed mode, build_moe_ffn is replaced by gRPC dispatch
// to Expert Nodes. The shared expert stays on Global Node always.
```

### ANDL Distributed FFN
In the ANDL distributed engine, `build_moe_ffn` is replaced by:

```
Global Node:
  1. Router computes top-8 expert indices + weights
  2. Hidden states + routes sent via gRPC ExpertCompute to Expert Nodes
  3. Expert Nodes compute FFN and return results
  4. Global Node merges with router weights
  5. Shared Expert computed locally
  6. moe_out + ffn_shexp → final FFN output
```

## Architecture Differences: Qwen3 vs Qwen3.5 vs Qwen3.6

| Feature | Qwen3-MoE | Qwen3.5-MoE | Qwen3.6-MoE |
|---|---|---|---|
| Attention types | Full only | Full + Linear | Full + Linear |
| Q/K normalization | No | Yes | Yes |
| Post-attention norm | No (uses ffn_norm) | attn_post_norm | attn_post_norm |
| Shared expert | No | Yes (ffn_gate/up/down_shexp + ffn_gate_inp_shexp) | Yes |
| Expert count | 128 | 128 | 256 |
| Top-k | 8 | 8 | 8 |
| Base class | `llm_graph_context` | `llm_build_delta_net_base` | `llm_build_delta_net_base` |
| ggml ops used | Standard attention | + ggml_ssm_conv, ggml_l2_norm | Same as 3.5 |
| IMRoPE sections | 4 | 4 | 4 |

## GQA (Grouped Query Attention)

Qwen3.6 uses 8:1 GQA ratio (16 Q heads, 2 KV heads):
```
n_head (Q)    = 16
n_head_kv (K) = 2
n_head_kv (V) = 2
head_dim      = hidden_dim / n_head = 2048 / 16 = 128
```

Full Attention weight shapes:
```
attn_q.weight:    [16 × 128 × 2, 2048] = [4096, 2048]  (Q + gate channel, Q8_0)
attn_k.weight:    [ 2 × 256, 2048]     = [512, 2048]   (Q8_0)
attn_v.weight:    [ 2 × 256, 2048]     = [512, 2048]   (Q8_0)
attn_output.weight: [2048, 2048]                        (Q8_0)
```

Q/K norm is applied per-256-element block (head_dim for normalization = attn_q_norm weight size = 256, covering Q + gate together). During attention, K/V heads are repeated/interleaved to match the 16 Q heads (8:1 ratio via ggml_repeat_4d).

## Qwen3.5-122B-A10B (48L, 256e, 3072d)

Large MoE variant. 48 layers (vs 40 on Qwen3.6-35B), 256 experts, 3072 embedding dim. Uses `llm_build_qwen35moe` (NOT qwen36moe) despite having 256 experts — the architecture string from GGUF is `qwen35moe`. Note: repo name is **A10B** (10B active), not A3B.

### moe-split Sharding for 122B

256 experts ÷ N shards. Per-node storage (trunk duplicated per shard):
- **3 shards**: ~85 experts each, ~26 GB/shard in Q4_K_M
- **4 shards**: 64 experts each, ~20 GB/shard
- **5 shards**: ~51 experts each, ~17 GB/shard

Each shard includes full 3072-dim trunk (embeddings, 48-layer attention/SSM/norms/shared-experts/routers) plus its expert group. Trunk dominates: ~70 GB of the 71.3 GB is non-expert weights. Expert-weight-per-shard is only ~1-2 GB.

⚠️ **VRAM constraint:** At Q4_K_M, a single shard (~20-26 GB for 3-4 split) exceeds 16 GB consumer GPUs. Options: (a) CPU-only on RAM-rich nodes, (b) IQ3_XXS quantization (smaller but may be broken — see memory), (c) more shards with more nodes, (d) partial GPU offload (-ngl 30-40).

### Verified Pipeline Benchmark (AVX2 CPU, Q4_K_XL, 72 GB)
24+24 layer split achieves 14.4× TTFT, 2.3× tok/s vs baseline. See andl-development → references/andl-122b-benchmark.md.

## Multimodal Support

**Qwen3.5 (all sizes including 122B) is a UNIFIED VISION-LANGUAGE model.** Official README confirms "Early fusion training on trillions of multimodal tokens" — vision capability is baked into model weights via early fusion, not a separate encoder. GGUF metadata: `image-text-to-text`.

**However, llama.cpp's `qwen35moe` architecture handler currently only supports text inference.** The image preprocessing and injection pathway for Qwen3.5's early fusion architecture is not implemented. Attempting `--image` with a Qwen3.5 model will result in the model responding that it cannot view images.

**Qwen3.6-MoE (35B-A3B)**: Multimodal status unverified. GGUF metadata check needed.

**Working multimodal options in llama.cpp:**
- **Qwen2.5-VL** family (3B, 7B, 32B, 72B) — separate vision encoder + mmproj, fully supported
- **Qwen3-VL** — models with dedicated vision encoders

See `distributed-moe-inference` skill → `references/qwen35-multimodal-capability.md` for full verification details.

Verified 2026-06-17:
- Official Qwen3.5 README: "Unified Vision-Language Foundation"
- GGUF metadata strings: `image-text-to-text`
- Actual inference test: model responded "I cannot view images" (llama.cpp limitation, not model limitation)

## Speculative Decoding for Qwen Models

### ngram Speculation: DO NOT USE for Dialogue

llama.cpp's `--spec-ngram-simple` (ngram blind speculation) has **0% acceptance rate for free-form dialogue/conversation**. It matches repeated n-gram patterns in the prompt context, which works for code generation and structured output, but fails completely for natural conversation due to diverse expression patterns. Always use a proper draft model (not ngram) for chat workloads.

### Vocab Compatibility (Draft Model Selection)

When selecting a draft model for speculative decoding, the tokenizer vocabulary MUST match. llama.cpp will reject draft models with incompatible vocabs at startup (error: `vocab mismatch`).

| Model Family | Vocab Size | Draft Compatible? |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen3 (all sizes) | **151,936** | ❌ NOT compatible with Qwen3.5/3.6 |
| Qwen3.5 (all sizes) | **248,320** | ✅ Compatible with Qwen3.5, Qwen3.6 |
| Qwen3.6 (all sizes) | 248,320 | ✅ Compatible with Qwen3.5 |

For Qwen3.5-122B (248K vocab), use a Qwen3.5-family draft model:
- **Qwen3.5-0.8B** (ideal — same gen, same vocab, ~0.8B params)
- Qwen3.5-4B (larger, slower draft but higher accuracy)
- Qwen3-0.6B is **NOT compatible** (151K ≠ 248K vocab)

For Qwen3, use Qwen3-family draft: Qwen3-0.6B, Qwen3-1.7B.

**Download sources for Qwen3.5-0.8B GGUF:**
- `unsloth/Qwen3.5-0.8B-GGUF` (Q4_K_M=507MB, Q8_0=1.1GB) — recommended
- `lmstudio-community/Qwen3.5-0.8B-GGUF`
- No official Qwen GGUF release; these are community conversions.

If downloading from HF mirror is slow, use aria2c for multi-connection resume:
```bash
aria2c -x 4 -s 4 -d /path/to/models/draft \
  -o Qwen3.5-0.8B-Q4_K_M.gguf \
  'https://hf-mirror.com/unsloth/Qwen3.5-0.8B-GGUF/resolve/main/Qwen3.5-0.8B-Q4_K_M.gguf'
```

Q8_0 is preferred for draft models (lossless → higher acceptance rate), but Q4_K_M at 507MB is a good tradeoff for bandwidth-constrained deployments.

## Pitfalls for ANDL Development

1. **QKV vs separated Q/K/V.** Linear attention layers use `wqkv` (merged), full attention layers use separate `wq/wk/wv`. The QKV split logic must check `is_recurrent(il)` — don't hardcode one or the other.

2. **Gate channel in Q projection.** Full attention layers have `wq` with shape `[n_head * head_dim * 2, hidden_dim]` — the second half is the gate, not part of Q. When splitting QKV, account for this.

3. **attn_post_norm vs ffn_norm.** Qwen3.6 has BOTH `attn_post_norm` (norm before FFN) AND `ffn_norm`. Older Qwen variants used `ffn_norm` as the post-attention norm. The naming is confusing but the architecture is clear: attention residual → attn_post_norm → MoE FFN → ffn_residual → ffn_norm.

4. **SSM state persistence.** The linear attention layers maintain persistent convolution/SSM state across tokens. In a distributed setting, this state lives on the Global Node and is NOT sent to Expert Nodes.

5. **Shared expert gating.** The shared expert has its own input gate (`ffn_gate_inp_shexp.weight`) that produces a per-token scalar via sigmoid. This is ADDED to the MoE output, not concatenated. The shared expert FFN follows the same SwiGLU pattern as expert FFNs.

6. **IMRoPE sections.** Qwen3.6 uses IMRoPE (type 40) with `rope.dimension_count=64` and `rope.dimension_sections=[11, 11, 10, 0]`. Sections sum to 32 (not 64), meaning only the first half of each RoPE-dimension block is sectioned. Don't confuse with MROPE (type 8) used by Qwen2-VL.

7. **Expert count doubled.** Qwen3.6 has 256 experts vs 128 in Qwen3.5-MoE. The ANDL sharding must account for this — with 8 shards, each Expert Node holds 32 experts (vs 16 for Qwen3.5).

## Overview

Qwen model family evolves from dense to MoE + hybrid attention. This skill focuses on architectural differences relevant to the ANDL distributed inference engine.

| Model | Type | Attention | MoE | llama.cpp class |
|---|---|---|---|---|

| Qwen3 | Dense | Full attention only | No | `llm_build_qwen3` |

| Qwen3.5 | Hybrid | Full + Linear (SSM/GDN) | No | `llm_build_qwen35` |
| Qwen3.5-MoE | Hybrid | Full + Linear (SSM/GDN) | Yes (128 experts) | `llm_build_qwen35moe` |

### Expert Sharding Strategy (ANDL)

256 experts ÷ 8 shards = 32 experts per shard.
Per-layer per-shard expert data: ~154+154+177 = ~485 MB (quantized).
All 40 layers per shard: ~19.4 GB total → **~2.4 GB per expert shard**.
All 8 shards: ~19.1 GB total expert weights.

Global Node total (embed + output + all attention + SSM + norms + routers + shared experts): **~2.5 GB**.

## Hybrid Attention System

### Layer Type Determination

```cpp
if (hparams.is_recurrent(il)) {
    // LINEAR ATTENTION LAYER: SSM/DeltaNet
    cur = build_layer_attn_linear(inp->get_recr(), cur, il);
} else {
    // FULL ATTENTION LAYER: Q/K/V + IMRoPE + sigmoid gate
    cur = build_layer_attn(inp->get_attn(), cur, inp_pos, sections, il);
}
```

The `is_recurrent(il)` check is determined by model hyperparameters loaded from GGUF metadata.

### Full Attention Layer (`build_layer_attn`)

```
Input → Q projection (wq) → Q/K Norm (attn_q_norm, attn_k_norm)
      → K projection (wk)  → IMRoPE on Q, K
      → V projection (wv)  → Attention compute
                           → Sigmoid gate (from Q projection's gate channel)
                           → Output projection (wo)
```

Key details:
- **Q projection outputs Q + gate**: `wq` shape is `[n_head * head_dim * 2, hidden_dim]` — the extra `head_dim` per head is the gate channel
- **Q/K normalization**: Q and K are individually RMS-normalized after projection (unique to Qwen3.5/3.6)
- **Sigmoid gating**: The gate channel is sigmoid-activated and multiplied element-wise with attention output

### Linear Attention Layer (`build_layer_attn_linear`)

```
Input → Merged QKV projection (wqkv) + Gate (wqkv_gate)
      → Beta projection (ssm_beta) → Sigmoid
      → Alpha projection (ssm_alpha) → Softplus → × ssm_a = gate
      → Conv1D (ssm_conv1d) on QKV
      → Q/K/L2-normed, split from conv output
      → DeltaNet attention (build_delta_net)
      → Gated normalization: norm(output, z) where z = silu(wqkv_gate)
      → Output projection (ssm_out)
```

This is a **gated delta net** (GDN) — a type of linear attention / state space model. It's computed on the Global Node, not distributed to experts.

### Convolution State Cache

Linear attention layers maintain a persistent conv state between tokens:
```cpp
conv_states_all  // shape: [(conv_kernel_size-1)*conv_channels, n_seqs]
ssm_states_all   // shape: [head_v_dim*head_v_dim*num_v_heads, n_seqs]
```

These are stored in `llm_build_delta_net_base`'s memory system and updated per-token via `ggml_cpy`.

## MoE Routing: Load-Balanced (Near-Uniform)

**Qwen3.6's routing is load-balanced by design.** Profiling on 468K tokens (626+ requests) from the iic/ms_agent dataset confirms near-perfect uniformity:

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Per-layer entropy | 7.68 bits (96% of theoretical max 8.0) |
| Experts used per layer | 256/256 — ALL used |
| Max expert hits | 23-24 (per request window) |
| Min expert hits | 12 |
| **Cold/hot ratio** | **Only 2:1** |
| 80% coverage needs | **~195/256 experts** (76%) |
| 95% coverage needs | **~239/256 experts** (93%) |
| 99.9% coverage needs | ~255/256 experts |
| Top-1 expert traffic share | ~0.5% |

**Layer 39 is special:** only 28/256 experts used, with just 96 total hits — this is the final layer and receives far fewer tokens due to early termination in the profiling corpus.

This means **hot/warm/cold expert tiering is ineffective for Qwen3.6** — ~76% of experts must be "hot" to cover even 80% of traffic. Compare to DeepSeek-V3 where ~15% of experts cover 80% of traffic with entropy ~5.5 bits. The model was trained with strong load-balancing loss to prevent router collapse.

For tiered deployment, consider models with more skewed routing (DeepSeek V3, Mixtral) or accept that Qwen3.6 needs all experts readily accessible. The practical approach for 16GB GPUs is **streaming per-layer** — keep all 256 experts in CPU RAM (192GB is plenty), load one layer's experts to GPU per inference step.

## MoE FFN Layer (`build_layer_ffn`)

```cpp
// 1. MoE expert routing (on Global Node)
moe_out = build_moe_ffn(cur,
    ffn_gate_inp,          // Router weight [256, 2048]
    ffn_up_exps,           // Expert up projections
    ffn_gate_exps,         // Expert gate projections
    ffn_down_exps,         // Expert down projections
    n_expert=256, n_expert_used=8,
    LLM_FFN_SILU,          // SiLU activation
    true,                  // use shared expert
    expert_weights_scale,  // from hparams
    LLAMA_EXPERT_GATING_FUNC_TYPE_SOFTMAX  // routing uses softmax
);

// 2. Shared expert (on Global Node)
if (ffn_up_shexp != nullptr) {
    ffn_shexp = build_ffn(cur, ffn_up/gate/down_shexp, LLM_FFN_SILU, LLM_FFN_PAR);
    shared_gate = sigmoid(ffn_gate_inp_shexp @ cur);  // token-level gate
    ffn_shexp = ffn_shexp * shared_gate;
    cur = moe_out + ffn_shexp;  // ADDITIVE merge!
}

// Note: In ANDL distributed mode, build_moe_ffn is replaced by gRPC dispatch
// to Expert Nodes. The shared expert stays on Global Node always.
```

### ANDL Distributed FFN
In the ANDL distributed engine, `build_moe_ffn` is replaced by:

```
Global Node:
  1. Router computes top-8 expert indices + weights
  2. Hidden states + routes sent via gRPC ExpertCompute to Expert Nodes
  3. Expert Nodes compute FFN and return results
  4. Global Node merges with router weights
  5. Shared Expert computed locally
  6. moe_out + ffn_shexp → final FFN output
```

## Architecture Differences: Qwen3 vs Qwen3.5 vs Qwen3.6

| Feature | Qwen3-MoE | Qwen3.5-MoE | Qwen3.6-MoE |
|---|---|---|---|
| Attention types | Full only | Full + Linear | Full + Linear |
| Q/K normalization | No | Yes | Yes |
| Post-attention norm | No (uses ffn_norm) | attn_post_norm | attn_post_norm |
| Shared expert | No | Yes (ffn_gate/up/down_shexp + ffn_gate_inp_shexp) | Yes |
| Expert count | 128 | 128 | 256 |
| Top-k | 8 | 8 | 8 |
| Base class | `llm_graph_context` | `llm_build_delta_net_base` | `llm_build_delta_net_base` |
| ggml ops used | Standard attention | + ggml_ssm_conv, ggml_l2_norm | Same as 3.5 |
| IMRoPE sections | 4 | 4 | 4 |

### Additional Qwen3.6-Specific Weights (vs Qwen3-MoE)

```

blk.{N}.attn_k_norm.weight       # K normalization (NEW in 3.5+)

blk.{N}.ffn_up_shexp.weight      # Shared expert up (NEW in 3.5+)

blk.{N}.ssm_conv1d.weight        # SSM convolution kernel (NEW in 3.5+)
blk.{N}.ssm_dt.weight            # SSM delta_t (NEW in 3.5+)

blk.{N}.ssm_beta.weight          # SSM beta (NEW in 3.5+)
blk.{N}.ssm_norm.weight          # SSM output norm (NEW in 3.5+)
blk.{N}.ssm_out.weight           # SSM output projection (NEW in 3.5+)
```

## GQA (Grouped Query Attention)

Qwen3.6 uses 8:1 GQA ratio (16 Q heads, 2 KV heads):
```
n_head (Q)    = 16
n_head_kv (K) = 2
n_head_kv (V) = 2
head_dim      = hidden_dim / n_head = 2048 / 16 = 128
```

Full Attention weight shapes:
```
attn_q.weight:    [16 × 128 × 2, 2048] = [4096, 2048]  (Q + gate channel, Q8_0)
attn_k.weight:    [ 2 × 256, 2048]     = [512, 2048]   (Q8_0)
attn_v.weight:    [ 2 × 256, 2048]     = [512, 2048]   (Q8_0)
attn_output.weight: [2048, 2048]                        (Q8_0)
```

Q/K norm is applied per-256-element block (head_dim for normalization = attn_q_norm weight size = 256, covering Q + gate together). During attention, K/V heads are repeated/interleaved to match the 16 Q heads (8:1 ratio via ggml_repeat_4d).

## Qwen3.5-122B-A10B (48L, 256e, 3072d)

Large MoE variant. 48 layers (vs 40 on Qwen3.6-35B), 256 experts, 3072 embedding dim. Uses `llm_build_qwen35moe` (NOT qwen36moe) despite having 256 experts — the architecture string from GGUF is `qwen35moe`. Note: repo name is **A10B** (10B active), not A3B.

head_dim (key/value_length): 256

### moe-split Sharding for 122B

256 experts ÷ N shards. Per-node storage (trunk duplicated per shard):
- **3 shards**: ~85 experts each, ~26 GB/shard in Q4_K_M
- **4 shards**: 64 experts each, ~20 GB/shard
- **5 shards**: ~51 experts each, ~17 GB/shard

Each shard includes full 3072-dim trunk (embeddings, 48-layer attention/SSM/norms/shared-experts/routers) plus its expert group. Trunk dominates: ~70 GB of the 71.3 GB is non-expert weights. Expert-weight-per-shard is only ~1-2 GB.

⚠️ **VRAM constraint:** At Q4_K_M, a single shard (~20-26 GB for 3-4 split) exceeds 16 GB consumer GPUs. Options: (a) CPU-only on RAM-rich nodes, (b) IQ3_XXS quantization (smaller but may be broken — see memory), (c) more shards with more nodes, (d) partial GPU offload (-ngl 30-40).

24+24 layer split achieves 14.4× TTFT, 2.3× tok/s vs baseline. See andl-development → references/andl-122b-benchmark.md.

## Multimodal Support

**Qwen3.5 (all sizes including 122B) is a UNIFIED VISION-LANGUAGE model.** Official README confirms "Early fusion training on trillions of multimodal tokens" — vision capability is baked into model weights via early fusion, not a separate encoder. GGUF metadata: `image-text-to-text`.

**However, llama.cpp's `qwen35moe` architecture handler currently only supports text inference.** The image preprocessing and injection pathway for Qwen3.5's early fusion architecture is not implemented. Attempting `--image` with a Qwen3.5 model will result in the model responding that it cannot view images.

**Qwen3.6-MoE (35B-A3B)**: Multimodal status unverified. GGUF metadata check needed.

**Working multimodal options in llama.cpp:**
- **Qwen2.5-VL** family (3B, 7B, 32B, 72B) — separate vision encoder + mmproj, fully supported
- **Qwen3-VL** — models with dedicated vision encoders

See `distributed-moe-inference` skill → `references/qwen35-multimodal-capability.md` for full verification details.

Verified 2026-06-17:
- Official Qwen3.5 README: "Unified Vision-Language Foundation"
- GGUF metadata strings: `image-text-to-text`
- Actual inference test: model responded "I cannot view images" (llama.cpp limitation, not model limitation)

## Speculative Decoding for Qwen Models

### ngram Speculation: DO NOT USE for Dialogue

llama.cpp's `--spec-ngram-simple` (ngram blind speculation) has **0% acceptance rate for free-form dialogue/conversation**. It matches repeated n-gram patterns in the prompt context, which works for code generation and structured output, but fails completely for natural conversation due to diverse expression patterns. Always use a proper draft model (not ngram) for chat workloads.

### Vocab Compatibility (Draft Model Selection)

When selecting a draft model for speculative decoding, the tokenizer vocabulary MUST match. llama.cpp will reject draft models with incompatible vocabs at startup (error: `vocab mismatch`).

| Model Family | Vocab Size | Draft Compatible? |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen3 (all sizes) | **151,936** | ❌ NOT compatible with Qwen3.5/3.6 |
| Qwen3.5 (all sizes) | **248,320** | ✅ Compatible with Qwen3.5, Qwen3.6 |
| Qwen3.6 (all sizes) | 248,320 | ✅ Compatible with Qwen3.5 |

For Qwen3.5-122B (248K vocab), use a Qwen3.5-family draft model:
- **Qwen3.5-0.8B** (ideal — same gen, same vocab, ~0.8B params)
- Qwen3.5-4B (larger, slower draft but higher accuracy)
- Qwen3-0.6B is **NOT compatible** (151K ≠ 248K vocab)

For Qwen3, use Qwen3-family draft: Qwen3-0.6B, Qwen3-1.7B.

**Download sources for Qwen3.5-0.8B GGUF:**
- `unsloth/Qwen3.5-0.8B-GGUF` (Q4_K_M=507MB, Q8_0=1.1GB) — recommended
- `lmstudio-community/Qwen3.5-0.8B-GGUF`
- No official Qwen GGUF release; these are community conversions.

If downloading from HF mirror is slow, use aria2c for multi-connection resume:
```bash
aria2c -x 4 -s 4 -d /path/to/models/draft \
  -o Qwen3.5-0.8B-Q4_K_M.gguf \
  'https://hf-mirror.com/unsloth/Qwen3.5-0.8B-GGUF/resolve/main/Qwen3.5-0.8B-Q4_K_M.gguf'
```

Q8_0 is preferred for draft models (lossless → higher acceptance rate), but Q4_K_M at 507MB is a good tradeoff for bandwidth-constrained deployments.

## Pitfalls for ANDL Development

1. **QKV vs separated Q/K/V.** Linear attention layers use `wqkv` (merged), full attention layers use separate `wq/wk/wv`. The QKV split logic must check `is_recurrent(il)` — don't hardcode one or the other.

2. **Gate channel in Q projection.** Full attention layers have `wq` with shape `[n_head * head_dim * 2, hidden_dim]` — the second half is the gate, not part of Q. When splitting QKV, account for this.

3. **attn_post_norm vs ffn_norm.** Qwen3.6 has BOTH `attn_post_norm` (norm before FFN) AND `ffn_norm`. Older Qwen variants used `ffn_norm` as the post-attention norm. The naming is confusing but the architecture is clear: attention residual → attn_post_norm → MoE FFN → ffn_residual → ffn_norm.

4. **SSM state persistence.** The linear attention layers maintain persistent convolution/SSM state across tokens. In a distributed setting, this state lives on the Global Node and is NOT sent to Expert Nodes.

5. **Shared expert gating.** The shared expert has its own input gate (`ffn_gate_inp_shexp.weight`) that produces a per-token scalar via sigmoid. This is ADDED to the MoE output, not concatenated. The shared expert FFN follows the same SwiGLU pattern as expert FFNs.

6. **IMRoPE sections.** Qwen3.6 uses IMRoPE (type 40) with `rope.dimension_count=64` and `rope.dimension_sections=[11, 11, 10, 0]`. Sections sum to 32 (not 64), meaning only the first half of each RoPE-dimension block is sectioned. Don't confuse with MROPE (type 8) used by Qwen2-VL.

7. **Expert count doubled.** Qwen3.6 has 256 experts vs 128 in Qwen3.5-MoE. The ANDL sharding must account for this — with 8 shards, each Expert Node holds 32 experts (vs 16 for Qwen3.5).
